peer_results.rationale: Candidates relate to TLAC/LTD requirements for U.S. GSIBs and intermediate holding company support agreements. These topics concern systemic resolution capacity and U.S. parent-subsidiary liquidity structures, which are structurally different from BAC's specific disclosure regarding the swap dealer registration and capital compliance of its European entities (MLI and BofASE).

comparisons.peer_summary: As a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, GSBE was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these roles as of both December 2024 and December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose the compliance status of their specific European entities acting as swap dealers and security-based swap dealers. BAC’s MLI and BofASE entities maintained net liquid assets and capital that exceeded minimum requirements at December 31, 2024. Similarly, GS’s GSBE entity was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these roles as of December 2024. Both disclosures confirm registration with both the SEC (as security-based swap dealers) and the CFTC (as swap dealers), indicating similar regulatory treatment for their European swap dealer operations.

sentences.text: In addition, MLI and BofASE remained conditionally registered with the SEC as security-based swap dealers, and maintained net liquid assets at December 31, 2024 that exceeded the applicable minimum requirements under the Exchange Act.
The entities are also registered as swap dealers with the CFTC and met applicable capital requirements at December 31, 2024.
GSBE is a registered swap dealer with the CFTC and a registered security-based swap dealer with the SEC.
As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GSBE was subject to and in compliance with applicable capital requirements for swap dealers and security-based swap dealers.

comparisons.peer_summary: As a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, GSI was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these roles as of both December 2024 and December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to BAC’s disclosure regarding its European entities, GS also reports compliance for another entity, GSI, which is registered as a swap dealer and security-based swap dealer. Like BAC, GS confirms that GSI was subject to and in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these roles at December 2024. This mirrors BAC's specific focus on the capital maintenance of conditionally registered SEC dealers and registered CFTC dealers in its European jurisdictions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory capital requirements for J.P. Morgan Securities
comparisons.peer_summary: J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to net capital requirements under the SEC's Net Capital Rule (Rule 15c3-1), has elected to compute minimum net capital using Alternative Net Capital Requirements, and as a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, must maintain tentative net capital above $5.0 billion and notify regulators if it falls below $6.0 billion.
comparisons.comparison: BAC and J.P. Morgan both disclose specific regulatory capital regimes for their subsidiaries registered as swap dealers and security-based swap dealers. BAC’s MLI and BofASE entities maintained net liquid assets exceeding Exchange Act minimums. J.P. Morgan Securities, also registered with both the SEC and CFTC as a security-based and swap dealer, is subject to alternative minimum net capital requirements under Rule 15c3-1, requiring it to hold tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion. Both disclosures highlight the distinct capital calculation methods (net liquid assets vs. tentative net capital) applicable to swap dealer registrations.

sentences.text: In addition, MLI and BofASE remained conditionally registered with the SEC as security-based swap dealers, and maintained net liquid assets at December 31, 2024 that exceeded the applicable minimum requirements under the Exchange Act.
The entities are also registered as swap dealers with the CFTC and met applicable capital requirements at December 31, 2024.
J.P. Morgan Securities is registered with the SEC as a security-based swap dealer and with the CFTC as a swap dealer.

As a result of additional SEC and CFTC capital and financial reporting requirements for security-based swap dealers and swap dealers, J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to alternative minimum net capital requirements and required to hold "tentative net capital" in excess of $5.0 billion.
J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to the regulatory capital requirements of Rule 15c3-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Net Capital Rule").
